conservation.notes: Least Concern overall, with a large global population (17-28 million in Europe alone, up to 120 million worldwide including feral and domestic descendants). The wild, undomesticated form is scarce and declining in Britain, largely through interbreeding with feral birds; it persists mainly on remote coasts and cliffs of northern and western Scotland (most strongly in the Outer Hebrides).

human_tolerance.notes: Compared to wild rock doves, feral pigeons are unafraid of humans owing to their long history of domestication, and are extremely trusting and tolerant of people; they gather in dense flocks around outdoor food, waste bins and people who feed them, and nest and roost on building ledges, eaves and under bridges as a substitute for natural cliffs.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: Can breed at any time of year (production of crop milk removes the usual dependence on a seasonal insect flush), with up to six clutches a year, but peak breeding is spring and summer when food is most abundant; exact start/end dates are a judgement placed around the described peak.

vocalizations.description: Soft, slightly wavering coo, 'crruoo-u', given year-round and especially during display, when it is accompanied by an inflated throat, tail fanning, strutting and bowing.
Grunt-like 'oorhh' alarm call given at the sight of a predator; a flushing bird also produces a loud, noisy wing-clap at take-off that cues other birds in the flock to fly.

common_names.note: en label follows the brief's instruction to record this as the feral urban form ('feral pigeon'); fr/de/nl labels are Wikidata's sitelink-derived labels for Q42326 (frwiki/dewiki/nlwiki, which cover the same biological species).

conservation.note: IUCN status and population figures from the Rock dove infobox/distribution section; the note on wild-type scarcity and Outer Hebrides refuge is quoted/paraphrased from the same article and 'The scarcity of the wild rock dove is largely due to interbreeding with feral birds' (Feral pigeon article).

range.note: Native list assembled from the Rock dove article's subspecies distributions (the natural, wild range): C. l. livia 'west, central Europe, north Africa to central Asia' (GB, IE, PT, ES, FR, IT, DE, BE, NL, CH, AT, MA, DZ, TN); C. l. gymnocycla 'Mauritania and Senegal to south Mali and Ghana' (MR, SN, ML, GH); C. l. targia 'north Mali and south Algeria to central Sudan' (SD); C. l. schimperi 'east Egypt, south Sudan and Eritrea' (EG, ER); C. l. palaestinae 'Sinai (Egypt) to Syria, to west and south Arabian Peninsula' (SY, SA); C. l. gaddi 'east Turkey to Uzbekistan, to west and north Afghanistan' (TR, UZ, AF); C. l. intermedia 'south India and Sri Lanka' (IN, LK); Pakistan from C. l. neglecta (PK). GB is included because the wild, undomesticated nominate subspecies still breeds on remote coasts and cliffs of northern and western Scotland. Introduced list is a judgement sample from 'introduced into most of the rest of the world aboard European ships from 1603 onwards' (major feral-only regions named or well documented: Americas, Australia, New Zealand, southern Africa, Japan), since Wikipedia does not give an exhaustive country list. This record covers the whole species Columba livia (wild + domestic + feral, which readily interbreed); the urban form this record is tuned for (traits, diet, habitat, human_tolerance) is specifically the feral, human-commensal population, which in GB and most of the modelled range descends from escaped/released domestic stock rather than the wild coastal population.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: 'Although it is a strong flier, it also glides frequently'; ground movement is described as a walking pace during courtship ('approaches the female at a rapid walking pace'). Pigeons characteristically walk (with the familiar head-bob) rather than hop, so 'Hop' is omitted; Glide is folded into Fly since the schema's locomotion set does not separate powered flight from gliding for a single flight mode animation.

traits.perching.note: Roosts and perches on cliff ledges in the wild and on building ledges, eaves, wires and bridges as a feral bird.

traits.nest_type.note: 'The nest is a flimsy platform of straw and sticks, laid on a ledge, under cover.'

traits.mass_kg.note: Midpoint of 'Weight for wild or feral rock doves ranges from 238-380 g.'

traits.mass_range_kg.note: 'Weight for wild or feral rock doves ranges from 238-380 g.'

traits.length_m.note: Midpoint of 'The adult of the nominate subspecies of the rock dove is 30 to 35 cm long.'

traits.lifespan_y.note: 'A rock dove's lifespan ranges from 3-5 years in the wild to 15 years in captivity, though longer-lived specimens have been reported.' Using the midpoint of the wild-lifespan range (4 years) as a typical wild/feral figure; this is not a mean survival estimate.

traits.diet.note: 'Rock doves are omnivorous, but prefer plant matter: chiefly fruit and grains ... naturally granivorous, eating seeds that fit down their gullet. They may sometimes consume small invertebrates such as worms or insect larvae as a protein supplement.' A semi-rural Kansas feral-pigeon diet study cited on the Feral pigeon page found 92% maize, 3.2% oats, 3.7% cherry, plus insects/spiders; maize and oats are mapped to the schema's 'seed' share and cherry to 'fruit'. Urban feral pigeons additionally scavenge discarded human food (bread, popcorn, cake, peanuts, currants) which the schema has no dedicated category for; it is folded into 'seed'/'fruit' as the closest available grain/plant-matter categories. Shares are therefore a rounded judgement, not a precise measurement.

traits.social.note: 'Pigeons are often found in pairs in the breeding season, but are often gregarious, living in flocks of 50 to 500 birds (dependent on the food supply).'

traits.activity_pattern.note: Described foraging, courtship and flocking behaviour all occur by day; no nocturnal activity is described.

traits.defense.note: 'When disturbed a pigeon within a flock will take off with a noisy clapping sound that cues for other pigeons to take to flight' -- the primary response to a threat (e.g. a peregrine falcon) is to flee by flight.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement from 'Compared to their wild relatives, feral pigeons are unafraid of humans due to their long history of domestication, and are extremely trusting and tolerant of people.' Set low, well below the wild rock dove's presumed wariness.

habitat.use.note: 'Pigeons feed on the ground in flocks or individually' and roost/perch on ledges and structures rather than trees; the schema has no dedicated 'building ledge' stratum, so time off the ground is folded into 'aerial' as the closest available category. Judgement split, not a sourced fraction.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Wild birds nest and roost in 'crevices' of cliffs, caves and canyons; feral birds use analogous crevices and recesses of buildings. 'cavity' is the closest ResourceTag to a ledge/crevice recess; there is no dedicated 'ledge' tag.

habitat.resources.note: Seed/fruit/invertebrate weights follow the diet shares above; nest_platform weight reflects the ledge-platform nest; perch weight reflects roosting/loafing on ledges, wires and rooftops; water weight reflects the described ability to 'dip their bills into the water and drink continuously' -- qualitative, not measured.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: urban_affinity, uses_gardens and the notes text follow the described commensal, food-scavenging urban lifestyle. light_max and flight_distance_m are judgement, reflecting the described extreme tolerance of people and the absence of a measured flight-initiation distance in the source.

seasonal.strategy.note: 'The species can breed at any time of the year due to their ability to produce crop milk'; no migration or dormancy is described.

seasonal.phases.note: 'Peak times are spring and summer, when the food supply is abundant enough to support embryonic egg development. Laying of eggs can take place up to six times per year.' Exact phase start/end dates are a judgement placed around the described peak.

seasonal.life_stages.note: 'Incubation, shared by both parents, lasts 17 to 19 days' (midpoint 18 used for Egg duration_days). 'Pigeons are altricial and their fledging period is about 30 days' (used for Juvenile duration_days); scale is a judgement approximation.

vocalizations.coo.note: 'The call is a soft, slightly wavering, coo crruoo-u.' 'When displaying, songs are partly sexual, partly threatening. They are accompanied by an inflated throat, tail fanning, strutting, and bowing.' Mapped to the schema's 'Song' context (the closest enum value to a display/pair-bonding call) since the schema has no dedicated 'Coo' context.

vocalizations.alarm_grunt.note: 'The alarm call, given at sight of predators, is a grunt-like oorhh.'

look.note: Modelled on the wild-type ('blue bar') plumage described as the ancestral and still most-recognised morph: 'dark bluish-grey head, neck, and chest feathers with glossy greenish to reddish-purple iridescence along its neck feathers... the two black bars on its pale grey wings are also distinctive... The iris is red-brown... The feet are red to pink.' Feral pigeons vary far more widely in colour (checkered, red, brown, white, pied) than this default, as both articles describe; that variation is not modelled. Proportions (stout body, short legs, small head, short stubby bill) and extra-part placement are judgement.

behavior.note: Authored parameters for the shared perching-songbird program: ground foraging on seed, a short flee distance reflecting extreme tolerance of people, a year-round nest-building window (nest_m1=1, nest_m2=12) reflecting the ability to breed at any time of year, and call ids matching the coo/alarm_grunt vocalizations above.
